Import CSL JSON files into Zotero

Source: R/csljson_to_zotero.R
csljson_to_zotero.Rd

Import one or more CSL JSON files (e.g. the chunks written by corpus_to_csljson()) into Zotero.

  • method = "local" sends the items to a running Zotero desktop app via its local connector endpoint (/connector/import, the endpoint the browser connector uses). Zotero's own CSL JSON importer does the mapping. Items go into the library or collection currently selected in Zotero; select a group library there to import into the group, and Zotero sync uploads them.

  • method = "web" (headless upload via the Zotero Web API) is not implemented yet and raises an error.

Zotero imports the CSL note into Extra; for files written by corpus_to_csljson() its first line is the item's OpenAlex: W....

Usage

csljson_to_zotero(
  files,
  method = c("local", "web"),
  existing = c("skip", "update", "overwrite"),
  tags = NULL,
  collection = NULL,
  url = "http://127.0.0.1:23119",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_LOCAL_API_KEY"),
  timeout = 3600
)

Arguments

files

Character vector. Paths to CSL JSON files. If a single element points to an existing directory, all *.json files in that directory (non-recursive) are used.

method

"local" (default) or "web". See Description.

existing

"skip" (default), "update" or "overwrite": what to do with items whose OpenAlex ID is already in the selected Zotero library. See "Items already in Zotero".

tags

NULL (default: no tags written), or a data.frame or path to a parquet file with columns openalex_id, tag and optionally type (0 manual, 1 automatic), such as the one written by zotero_tags(). See "Tags".

collection

NULL (default: only the target selected in Zotero), or the path of a collection to put the works in, e.g. c("my_project", "corpus_a"). See "Collection".

url

Base URL of the local Zotero server. Default "http://127.0.0.1:23119".

api_key

Key for Zotero's local API, only needed for existing = "update" or "overwrite", tags or collection. Defaults to Sys.getenv("ZOTERO_LOCAL_API_KEY"); if empty, Zotero is asked for one.

timeout

Seconds to wait for Zotero to import one file. Default 3600; a 10000-item chunk can take 10 to 30 minutes (see "Speed").

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame with one row per file and columns:

file

Path to the CSL JSON file.

status_code

HTTP status code of the last import request (201 on success, NA if nothing had to be imported).

ok

Logical; TRUE if every step for the file succeeded.

n_items

Number of new items imported.

n_skipped

Number of items skipped because they already exist.

n_updated

Number of existing Zotero items updated or overwritten.

n_tagged

Number of items whose tags were written from tags.

message

Character; error text if something failed.

Items already in Zotero

Before importing, the selected library (all of it, not only the selected collection) is searched for items whose Extra holds an OpenAlex ID, in any of the forms in use: OpenAlex: W... (written by this package), OpenAlex: https://openalex.org/W... (Zotero's OpenAlex translators), openalex.work_id: W... and OpenAlex Work ID: W... (two Zotero plugins). Items whose OpenAlex ID is not found there (or that have none) are imported. Items already there are handled by existing:

  • "skip" (default): left untouched and not imported.

  • "update": the existing Zotero item gets the new metadata; fields the new metadata does not have keep their old values.

  • "overwrite": all fields of the existing Zotero item are replaced by the new metadata; fields it does not have are emptied.

With "update" and "overwrite" the existing item keeps its item key, child notes and attachments, tags, collections and related items. Technically, the items are imported with Zotero's CSL JSON importer, their fields are copied onto the existing items, and the imported copies are deleted again.

Tags

CSL JSON has no tags, so by default items arrive without tags, and existing items keep theirs. With tags (e.g. the zotero_tags.parquet written by zotero_tags()), tags are written by OpenAlex ID, following existing:

  • new items get the tags of their OpenAlex ID;

  • "skip": existing items are left untouched, tags included;

  • "update": tags missing on the existing item are added, its own are kept;

  • "overwrite": the existing item's tags are replaced by those in tags, and removed if tags has none for its OpenAlex ID.

Rows of several libraries are merged; a tag keeps its type (manual or automatic).

Collection

With collection, e.g. c("my_project", "corpus_a"), the works are also put into that collection, nested from the top level of the selected library (my_project > corpus_a). Missing collections are created, existing ones of the same name reused, so a re-export goes into the same collection. Works already in the library join the collection too, with every value of existing: collections are independent of the item, and one work can be in several. Other collections of an item are kept.

New items also land in whatever is selected in Zotero, so select the library itself (not a collection) to have them only in collection. Deleting the collection in Zotero with its items removes an accidental export again; items that were already in the library before stay in their other collections.

Write access

"update", "overwrite", tags and collection write through Zotero's local API, which needs Zotero 10 or later and a key. If api_key is empty, Zotero shows a dialog asking to allow access for "openalexConvert": choose Always Allow (a key allowed once is only good for a single write). The key is kept for the rest of the R session.

Progress is reported via the progressr package.

Speed

Zotero gets slower as the library grows. Measured with Zotero 10.0.6 on a Mac, importing 5000 works in files of 1000 into a library starting at about 440 items:

fileitems in library beforetimeworks/s
144057 s17.5
2144089 s11.2
32440121 s8.3
43440145 s6.9
54440163 s6.1

Zotero's memory use grew to 3.4 GB during that run. For 100000 works, plan for several hours to more than a day, and consider restarting Zotero every few files.

The search for items already in the library (run once per call, for every value of existing) took 0.2 s for 369 IDs and 6.6 s for 5369; it grows faster than the library, so expect tens of minutes for 100000. Re-running all 5000 works with existing = "skip" took 4.7 s, mostly that search. corpus_to_csljson() itself takes about 1 ms per work.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In Zotero, select the target library or collection first.
res <- csljson_to_zotero("csljson")  # directory with chunk_1.json, ...
subset(res, !ok)

# Re-export after the corpus was updated: refresh what is already there
csljson_to_zotero("csljson", existing = "update")
} # }
